title: Chipping and putting before your tee shot
question: Is it allowed to chip or putt on or near the teeing area while waiting for your turn to play?

choices.text: Yes, you are allowed to practise chipping or putting there.
No, you must wait without playing any shots.
Only if no one else is waiting to play.
Only if your coach is present.

explanation: You are allowed to practise chipping or putting on or near the teeing area while waiting to tee off, provided it doesn't delay play.
imagePrompt: A left-handed teenage boy practises a chip shot with a wedge on the grass next to the tee markers, waiting for his turn.
imageAlt: Teenage boy chipping the ball near the tee markers before starting his round.

issues: Golfer is set up as right-handed, not left-handed as required (left hand is higher, not lower; facing direction for a right-handed chip shot).
Club posture and hand placement do not match left-handed setup.
The scene itself looks believable for golf and all other visual requirements (attire, club, ball, course elements) are met.
Only one visible golf ball and one realistic wedge present.
Tee marker is visible and course setting is plausible.
Golfer's posture is physically plausible for a chip, but only for a right-handed golfer.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Change the golfer's setup to left-handed: ensure the golfer is facing the opposite direction, with the right hand lower on the grip, addressing the ball naturally for a left-handed chip shot. Clothing, skin tone, and club details are correct; do not change these.
